p.src: Now Dong Zhuo wished to kill Yuan Shao, but Li Ru stopped him, saying, “The matter is not yet settled; you must not kill him rashly.” Sword in hand, Yuan Shao took leave of the assembled officials and departed. He hung his insignia of office upon the eastern gate and fled to Ji Province. Dong Zhuo said to Grand Tutor Yuan Wei, “Your nephew has behaved insolently. For your sake, I shall pardon him for the present. What say you to the matter of deposition and enthronement?” Yuan Wei replied, “The Grand Commandant’s judgment is correct.” Dong Zhuo declared, “Anyone who dares obstruct this great resolution shall be dealt with under military law.” The ministers trembled in fear and all said, “We shall obey your honored command in all things.” When the banquet was over, Dong Zhuo asked Palace Attendant Zhou Bi and Commandant Wu Qiong, “What will come of Yuan Shao’s departure?” Zhou Bi replied, “Yuan Shao departed in indignation. If you press the pursuit of him, he will inevitably rebel. Moreover, the Yuan clan has bestowed favors for four generations, and its former pupils and officers are spread throughout the realm. Should he gather men of prowess and assemble followers, heroes everywhere will rise in response, and the lands east of the mountains will no longer be yours. It would be better to pardon him and appoint him governor of a commandery. Delighted to have escaped punishment, Yuan Shao will surely cause no trouble.” Wu Qiong said, “Yuan Shao is fond of schemes but lacks decision; he is not worth fearing. Yet it would indeed be best to grant him the governorship of a commandery and thereby win the people’s hearts.”

p.src: Dong Zhuo followed their advice and that very day sent a messenger to appoint Yuan Shao Governor of Bohai. On the first day of the ninth month, he invited the Emperor to ascend the Jiade Hall and convened a great assembly of civil and military officials. Dong Zhuo drew his sword and, holding it before the assembly, declared, “The Son of Heaven is foolish and weak, and unfit to rule the realm. I have here an edict that ought now to be read aloud.” He then ordered Li Ru to read the edict: “Emperor Xiaoling departed early from his ministers and people. The Emperor succeeded to the throne, and all within the seas looked up to him with hope. Yet His Majesty is by nature frivolous, neglectful of proper dignity, and indolent in mourning. His want of virtue is now manifest, disgracing the exalted throne. The Empress Dowager has failed to show the conduct proper to a mother and has thrown the government into disorder. The Dowager Empress of Yongle died suddenly, leaving public opinion filled with doubt. Can it be that the Way of the Three Bonds, the great order of Heaven and Earth, has been found wanting? Prince Xie of Chenliu possesses abundant sage virtue and maintains a solemn regard for all rules of conduct. In mourning he has shown heartfelt grief, and no improper word has passed his lips. His fair name and excellent reputation are known throughout the realm. He should inherit the great enterprise and establish the imperial succession for ten thousand generations. The present Emperor is hereby deposed and made Prince of Hongnong, while the Empress Dowager shall return the governance. Let Prince Xie of Chenliu be respectfully enthroned as Emperor, in accord with Heaven and the people, thereby fulfilling the hopes of all living souls.”

p.src: When Li Ru had finished reading the edict, Dong Zhuo shouted to his attendants to help the Emperor down from the hall, remove his imperial seals and cords, and make him kneel for a long while facing north, proclaiming himself a subject and awaiting commands. He also ordered the Empress Dowager to remove her ceremonial robes and await further decree. The Emperor and Empress Dowager both wailed aloud. Every minister was stricken with grief. From below the steps, a high minister cried out furiously, “Traitor Dong Zhuo! How dare you devise this plot to deceive Heaven? I shall spatter you with the blood of my neck!” Brandishing the ivory court tablet in his hand, he struck straight at Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo flew into a rage and ordered the guards to seize him. It was Ding Guan, a Director of the Imperial Secretariat. Dong Zhuo ordered that he be dragged outside and beheaded. p.src: Dong Zhuo invited the Prince of Chenliu to ascend the throne hall. After the assembled ministers had offered their congratulations, Dong Zhuo ordered Empress Dowager He, the Prince of Hongnong, and his consort Lady Tang to be escorted to Yong’an Palace and confined there. The palace gates were sealed, and the ministers were forbidden to enter without authorization. Pitiably, the Young Emperor had ascended the throne in the fourth month, only to be deposed in the ninth. The Prince of Chenliu whom Dong Zhuo enthroned was Xie, courtesy name Bohe, the middle son of Emperor Ling. He was Emperor Xian, and was then nine years old. The era name was changed to Chuping. Dong Zhuo became Chancellor of State. At court he was accorded praise without being named, was exempted from hastening into the imperial presence, and was permitted to ascend the hall wearing sword and shoes. None could rival his power to grant favor or inflict punishment. Li Ru urged Dong Zhuo to promote renowned scholars and thereby win public esteem, and so recommended the talents of Cai Yong. Dong Zhuo summoned him, but Cai Yong did not answer the call. Enraged, Dong Zhuo sent someone to tell him, “If you do not come, I shall exterminate your clan.” Cai Yong was afraid and had no choice but to obey the summons and come. Dong Zhuo was overjoyed to see him. Within one month he promoted him three times, appointed him Palace Attendant, and treated him with exceptional intimacy and favor.

p.src: Dong Zhuo constantly sent men to spy upon them. That day, one of his spies obtained the poem and brought it to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo said, “He has written a poem expressing resentment. Now there is just cause to kill him.” He therefore ordered Li Ru to take ten armed guards into the palace and murder the Emperor. The Emperor was upstairs with the Empress Dowager and his consort when a palace maid announced Li Ru’s arrival. The Emperor was greatly alarmed. Li Ru presented the Emperor with poisoned wine, and the Emperor asked why. Li Ru replied, “The spring day is mild and harmonious, and Chancellor Dong has specially offered this wine to wish you long life.” The Empress Dowager said, “If you call it a wine of longevity, then you may drink first.” Li Ru said angrily, “Will you not drink?” He called his attendants to place a dagger and a length of white silk before them, saying, “If you will not drink the wine of longevity, you may choose these two things!” Consort Tang knelt and pleaded, “Let me drink the wine in the Emperor’s stead. Li Ru pressed the Emperor to drink, but the Emperor said, “Allow me to bid farewell to the Empress Dowager.” Then, weeping bitterly, he composed a song. His song ran:

p.src: When the songs were ended, they embraced one another and wept. Li Ru rebuked them, “The Chancellor is waiting for my report. Whom do you expect to rescue you by delaying like this?” The Empress Dowager cursed him loudly: “The traitor Dong has driven my son and me to this extremity, and August Heaven gives us no protection! You who aid his evil shall surely see your clans exterminated!” Li Ru flew into a rage. Seizing the Empress Dowager with both hands, he hurled her down from the tower. He ordered the guards to strangle Consort Tang and forced poisoned wine down the Young Emperor’s throat, killing him, then returned to report to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo ordered them buried outside the city. From then on, he entered the palace every night, violated the palace women, and slept upon the imperial bed. Once he led his army out of the city and came to the district of Yangcheng. It was the second month, and the villagers were holding a festival for the local gods. Men and women had all gathered there. Dong Zhuo ordered his soldiers to surround them and slaughter every one, plundered the women and property, and loaded them upon carts. More than a thousand severed heads were hung beneath the carts as the convoy returned to the capital, proclaiming that they had won a great victory over rebels. Below the city gate they burned the heads and distributed the women and property among the troops.

p.src: Wu Fu, Commandant of the Yue Cavalry, courtesy name Deyu, was filled with anger and indignation at Dong Zhuo’s brutality. He would wear a light coat of armor beneath his court robes and conceal a dagger, awaiting a chance to kill Dong Zhuo. One day, when Dong Zhuo entered the court, Wu Fu met him beneath the palace gallery, drew his dagger, and stabbed straight at him. Dong Zhuo was immensely strong and seized him with both hands. Lü Bu then rushed in and wrestled Wu Fu to the ground. Dong Zhuo demanded, “Who taught you to rebel?” Wu Fu glared at him and shouted, “You are no lord of mine, nor am I your subject. How can this be called rebellion? Your crimes and wickedness reach to Heaven, and every person longs to put you to death! My only regret is that I cannot tear you apart between chariots and thereby make amends to the realm!” Dong Zhuo flew into a rage and ordered that he be dragged outside and dismembered. Wu Fu continued cursing him until the moment of death. A poet of later times praised him in these lines:

p.src: Wang Yun received the letter and pondered it, but could devise no plan. One day, seeing all the veteran ministers gathered in the waiting chamber at court, Wang Yun said, “Today is this old man’s humble birthday. May I trouble you all to come to my residence this evening for a modest drink?” The officials all replied, “We shall certainly come to wish you long life.” That evening Wang Yun laid a banquet in the rear hall, and all the lords and high ministers attended. After several rounds of wine, Wang Yun suddenly covered his face and wept aloud. The startled officials asked, “On the honored occasion of the Minister’s birthday, why are you overcome with grief?” Wang Yun said, “Today is not in fact my birthday. I wished to gather with you all, but feared arousing Dong Zhuo’s suspicions, and so used that as a pretext. Dong Zhuo deceives the sovereign and usurps authority; the dynasty may not survive from one day to the next. Think how the Great Founder destroyed Qin and overthrew Chu, and thereby came to possess the whole realm; who could have imagined that, passed down to this day, it would now be lost at Dong Zhuo’s hands? That is why I weep.” At this, all the officials began to weep. But one man among them clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying, “Even if every lord and minister at court wept from night until dawn and from dawn until night, could you ever weep Dong Zhuo to death?” Wang Yun looked and saw that it was Cao Cao, Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry. Wang Yun said angrily, “Your forefathers too received stipends from the Han court. Instead of thinking how to repay the state, do you laugh at us?” Cao Cao replied, “I laugh at nothing else; I laugh because not one of you has a plan to kill Dong Zhuo. Though I possess little ability, I am willing to cut off Dong Zhuo’s head at once and hang it above the capital gate, thereby making amends to all under Heaven.” Wang Yun left his mat and asked, “What worthy plan have you, Mengde?” Cao Cao said, “Of late I have humbled myself to serve Dong Zhuo solely because I seek an opportunity to destroy him. Dong Zhuo now places considerable trust in me, and I can therefore approach him at favorable moments. I have heard that the Minister possesses a precious Seven-Star Dagger. Lend it to me, I pray, that I may enter the Chancellor’s residence and assassinate him. Even if I die, I shall have no regret!” Wang Yun said, “Mengde, if you truly possess such resolve, it is a great blessing for all under Heaven!” He then personally poured wine and presented it to Cao Cao. Cao Cao poured a libation and swore an oath, whereupon Wang Yun fetched the precious dagger and gave it to him. Cao Cao concealed the dagger, finished his wine, then rose, took leave of the officials, and departed. The officials remained seated a while longer, then dispersed as well.

p.src: The next day, Cao Cao strapped on the precious dagger and went to the Chancellor’s residence, where he asked for the Chancellor. An attendant said, “He is in the small pavilion.” Cao Cao went straight in to see him. Dong Zhuo sat upon a couch, with Lü Bu standing in attendance beside him. Dong Zhuo said, “Mengde, why have you come so late?” Cao Cao replied, “My horse is feeble and travels slowly.” Dong Zhuo turned to Lü Bu and said, “I have some fine horses sent from Xiliang. Fengxian, go personally and select one mount to bestow upon Mengde.” Lü Bu accepted the order and left. Cao Cao thought secretly, “This villain is fated to die!” He was about to draw the dagger and stab him. But fearing Dong Zhuo’s great strength, he dared not act rashly. Dong Zhuo, being very corpulent and unable to sit for long, lay down and turned his face toward the inside. Again Cao Cao thought, “Now this villain’s end has come!” He swiftly drew the precious dagger into his hand. Just as he was about to strike, Dong Zhuo happened to look up at the full-length mirror and saw Cao Cao drawing a dagger behind him. He wheeled round and demanded, “Mengde, what are you doing?”

Cao Cao, thrown into panic, held up the dagger, knelt, and said, “I possess a precious dagger and present it to my gracious Chancellor.” Dong Zhuo took it and examined it. Cao Cao removed the scabbard and gave it to Lü Bu. Dong Zhuo led Cao Cao out of the pavilion to inspect the horse. Cao Cao thanked him and said, “If I may borrow it, I should like to try riding it.” Dong Zhuo ordered that saddle and bridle be provided. Cao Cao led the horse out of the Chancellor’s residence, applied the whip, and galloped southeastward. Lü Bu said to Dong Zhuo, “Just now Cao Cao appeared to be about to assassinate you. When you challenged him and exposed him, he therefore pretended that he was presenting the dagger.” Dong Zhuo said, “I suspect as much myself.”

p.src: While they were speaking, Li Ru happened to arrive, and Dong Zhuo told him what had occurred. Li Ru said, “Cao Cao has neither wife nor children in the capital and lives alone in his lodgings. Send someone to summon him now. If he comes at once without misgivings, then he truly meant to present the dagger; but if he makes excuses and refuses to come, then he certainly attempted an assassination, and we may seize and interrogate him.” Dong Zhuo approved his words and immediately sent four jailers to summon Cao Cao. After a long while they returned and reported, “Cao Cao never returned to his lodgings. He galloped out through the eastern gate. When the gate officers questioned him, Cao Cao said, ‘The Chancellor has sent me on urgent official business,’ then gave his horse free rein and rode away.” Li Ru said, “The villain Cao Cao has fled with a guilty heart. There is no doubt he attempted to assassinate you.” Dong Zhuo said in a great rage, “I placed such trust in him, yet he sought to harm me!” Li Ru said, “He must have accomplices. Once Cao Cao is captured, we shall learn who they are.” Dong Zhuo therefore ordered notices circulated everywhere, bearing Cao Cao’s portrait and description and commanding his arrest. Whoever captured and delivered him would receive a thousand pieces of gold and be enfeoffed as a marquis of ten thousand households; whoever harbored him would suffer the same punishment as he.

u.src: While they were speaking, Li Ru happened to arrive, and Dong Zhuo told him what had occurred.
Li Ru said, “Cao Cao has neither wife nor children in the capital and lives alone in his lodgings.
Send someone to summon him now. If he comes at once without misgivings, then he truly meant to present the dagger;
but if he makes excuses and refuses to come, then he certainly attempted an assassination, and we may seize and interrogate him.”
Dong Zhuo approved his words and immediately sent four jailers to summon Cao Cao.
After a long while they returned and reported, “Cao Cao never returned to his lodgings. He galloped out through the eastern gate.
When the gate officers questioned him, Cao Cao said, ‘The Chancellor has sent me on urgent official business,’ then gave his horse free rein and rode away.”
Li Ru said, “The villain Cao Cao has fled with a guilty heart. There is no doubt he attempted to assassinate you.”
Dong Zhuo said in a great rage, “I placed such trust in him, yet he sought to harm me!”
Li Ru said, “He must have accomplices. Once Cao Cao is captured, we shall learn who they are.”
Dong Zhuo therefore ordered notices circulated everywhere, bearing Cao Cao’s portrait and description and commanding his arrest.
Whoever captured and delivered him would receive a thousand pieces of gold and be enfeoffed as a marquis of ten thousand households;
whoever harbored him would suffer the same punishment as he.

p.src: Now Cao Cao, having escaped beyond the city walls, raced toward Qiao Commandery. Passing through Zhongmu County, he was seized by soldiers guarding the pass and taken before the magistrate. Cao Cao said, “I am a traveling merchant. My surname is Huangfu.” The magistrate scrutinized Cao Cao, pondered for a long while, then said, “When I sought office in Luoyang, I once knew you as Cao Cao. Why conceal your identity? Take him to the cells for now. Tomorrow we shall escort him to the capital and claim the reward.” He rewarded the soldiers from the pass with wine and food and dismissed them.

p.src: At midnight the magistrate ordered a trusted attendant to bring Cao Cao out secretly and took him directly to the rear courtyard for questioning. He asked, “I hear the Chancellor treated you generously. Why have you brought this calamity upon yourself?” Cao Cao replied, “‘How can sparrows understand the aspirations of a great swan?’ Since you have captured me, you should escort me away and claim your reward.” The magistrate dismissed everyone around them and said to Cao Cao, “Do not underestimate me. I am no common petty official; I have merely not yet encountered a lord worthy of my service.” Cao Cao said, “For generations my forefathers have received stipends from the Han. If I gave no thought to repaying the state, how would I differ from a beast? I humbled myself to serve Dong Zhuo only because I sought an opportunity to destroy him and rid the state of this scourge. That the attempt has now failed is the will of Heaven!” The magistrate said, “Mengde, where do you intend to go on this journey?” Cao Cao replied, “I shall return to my native district, issue a forged imperial edict, and summon the lords throughout the realm to raise armies and destroy Dong Zhuo together. That is my desire.”

p.src: On hearing this, the magistrate personally untied Cao Cao, helped him into the seat of honor, bowed twice, and said, “You, sir, are truly a loyal and righteous man of the realm!” Cao Cao bowed in return and asked the magistrate’s name. The magistrate said, “My surname is Chen, my given name Gong, and my courtesy name Gongtai. My aged mother, wife, and children are all in Dong Commandery. Moved by your loyalty and righteousness, I am willing to abandon my office and flee with you.” Cao Cao was greatly delighted. That night Chen Gong gathered traveling expenses, and he and Cao Cao changed their clothes and disguises. Each carrying a sword on his back, they mounted horses and set out for Cao Cao’s native district.

p.src: After traveling for three days, they reached the Chenggao region as evening drew near. Cao Cao pointed with his whip toward a dense wood and said to Chen Gong, “A man named Lü Boshe lives here. He is my father’s sworn brother. What say you to visiting him for news of my family and seeking lodging for the night?” Chen Gong said, “That would be best.” The two dismounted before the manor and went in to see Lü Boshe. Lü Boshe said, “I heard that the court has circulated notices everywhere and is hunting you most urgently. Your father has already taken refuge in Chenliu. How did you manage to come here?” Cao Cao told him all that had happened and said, “Had it not been for Magistrate Chen, my bones would already have been ground to dust.” Lü Boshe bowed to Chen Gong and said, “Had it not been for your lordship, my young nephew and the entire Cao clan would have been destroyed. Please set your mind at ease and remain seated. You may lodge in my humble dwelling tonight.” After saying this, he rose and went inside. After a long while he emerged and said to Chen Gong, “There is no good wine in my house. Allow me to go to the western village and buy a jar with which to entertain you.” With that, he hurriedly mounted a donkey and departed.

p.src: Cao Cao and Chen Gong had been sitting for some time when they suddenly heard the sound of knives being sharpened behind the manor. Cao Cao said, “Lü Boshe is no close kinsman of mine. There is something suspicious about his departure. We should listen in secret.” The two crept behind the thatched hall and heard someone say, “How about binding him and killing him?” Cao Cao said, “Just as I thought! If we do not strike first now, we shall surely be captured.” He and Chen Gong drew their swords and rushed straight in. Sparing neither man nor woman, they killed all eight members of the household. When they searched as far as the kitchen, however, they found a pig tied up and ready for slaughter. Chen Gong said, “Mengde, your suspicious nature has led us to kill innocent people by mistake!” They hurried out of the manor, mounted their horses, and rode away. Before they had gone two li, they saw Boshe approaching on a donkey, two jars of wine hanging from the front of its saddle and fruit and vegetables in his hands. He called out, “Worthy nephew, Your Excellency, why are you leaving so soon?” Cao Cao replied, “I am a man under accusation and cannot remain long in one place.” Boshe said, “I have already instructed my family to slaughter a pig and entertain you. Worthy nephew, Your Excellency, why begrudge staying a single night? Please turn your horses around at once.”

p.src: Cao Cao paid him no heed and spurred his horse onward. After riding only a few paces, he suddenly drew his sword and turned back, calling to Boshe, “Who is that coming this way?” As Boshe turned his head to look, Cao Cao swung his sword and struck him down from the donkey. Chen Gong cried in astonishment, “What happened just now was a mistake—but why did you do this?” Cao Cao replied, “When Boshe returns home and sees so many people slain, how could he possibly let the matter rest? If he gathers men and pursues us, disaster will surely befall us.” Chen Gong said, “To kill him knowingly and deliberately is a monstrous injustice!” Cao Cao said, “I would rather betray all under Heaven than let anyone under Heaven betray me.” Chen Gong fell silent.

p.src: That night, after traveling several li, they knocked at the door of an inn beneath the bright moon and sought lodging. After the horses had been fed their fill, Cao Cao went to sleep first. Chen Gong pondered, “I thought Cao Cao was a good man, and so abandoned my office to follow him; but he is in truth a ruthless wretch! If I let him live today, he will surely bring calamity in the future.” He was about to draw his sword and kill Cao Cao. Indeed:
